diagnosis_line: Diagnosis: Bacterial stem and fruit canker on a tomato leaf (model confidence 92%). Estimated spread on the photographed leaf: medium.

llama.raw_text: Small, water soaked spots with white halo on fruits. Centre of spots become slightly raised, tan coloured and rough. Cankers develop and form cracks; slimy bacterial ooze through cracks. Vascular discolouration.

llama.raw_text: Small, brown, water-soaked, circular spots with yellow halo on leaves; older leaves fall. Small water-soaked spots on green fruit; the centre of the spots becomes irregular, light brown, sunken and scabby.

llama.raw_text: Lower leaves may drop before wilting. Pathogen is mostly confined to vascular region; in advantage cases, it may invade the cortex and pith and cause yellow brown discolouration of tissues.

diagnosis_line: Diagnosis: Collar rot on a tomato leaf (model confidence 92%). Estimated spread on the photographed leaf: medium.

llama.raw_text: Soft tissue necrosis of the stem bark near the soil line is the first sign of the disease. A white, cottony, and silvery mycelial growth is visible on the affected area. Later, a white to light brown mustard-like sclerotium appears on the same area. The disease is soil-borne and the pathogen survives in the form of sclerotia.

diagnosis_line: Diagnosis: Early blight on a tomato leaf (model confidence 92%). Estimated spread on the photographed leaf: medium.

llama.raw_text: Brown spots with concentric rings in a bull's eye pattern with a yellow margin. Fruit gets infected through the calyx or stem attachment; brown concentric rings on fruits. Irregular leaf spots mostly appear from the marginal portion of leaves. In many tomato cultivars, symptoms are V-shaped and progress towards the midrib. These lesions are having prominent yellowing on their outer margin due to a host-specific toxin produced by the pathogen. Mostly disease appears in the vegetative phase of the plant growth before flowering. This is a common disease of tomatoes occurring on the foliage at any stage of the growth. The fungus attacks the foliage causing characteristic leaf spots and blight. Early blight is first observed on the plants as small, black lesions mostly on the older foliage.

diagnosis_line: Diagnosis: Fruit rots on a tomato leaf (model confidence 92%). Estimated spread on the photographed leaf: medium.

dropped_sentences: Ensure proper drainage in the field.
llama.raw_text: Rhizoctonia fruit rot is the most serious disease of kharif tomatoes. Symptoms appear as rhythmic rotting of fruits coming with the soil contact. Rotting is followed by cracking and fungal growth over it. Lower portion of fruits are usually infected which come into contact with the soil. To prevent the disease, keep the fruits off the soil by staking the plants. Ensure proper drainage in the field.

llama.raw_text: Clearing of the veinlets and yellowing of the lower leaves. Younger leaves die in succession. Petiole and leaves droop and wilt. Browning of vascular system. Entire plant wilt and die.

diagnosis_line: Diagnosis: Grey leaf spot on a tomato leaf (model confidence 92%). Estimated spread on the photographed leaf: medium.

llama.raw_text: Small circular dark brown necrotic, numerous spots appear all over the leaf lamina that is uniformly distributed on entire foliage. Sometimes clear narrow yellow halo is visible around the spots. Usually these spots are isolated but in later stage they coalesce to each other. Severely infected older leaves blight and fall down.

diagnosis_line: Diagnosis: Late blight on a tomato leaf (model confidence 92%). Estimated spread on the photographed leaf: medium. This disease is urgent: it spreads very fast.

llama.raw_text: White sporulation on leaves. Blight appears on foliage as light-pale green water soaked dead area. Lesions are wet in morning and dried, shriveled in daylight. In moist and cloudy weather a downy white fungus develops near the outer margin of the lesion on the underside of the leaves.

diagnosis_line: An insect pest was found on the tomato plant: Red spider mite.

dropped_sentences: Affected leaves turn reddish brown and bronzy.
llama.raw_text: Affected leaves turn reddish brown and bronzy. Severe infestation leaves silken webbing on the leaves, wither and dry. Flower and fruit formation are affected. Red spider mites thrive in high temperatures, dry weather, and protected conditions. They are found on the lower surface of older leaves. When infestation is severe, they attack all parts of the plant. Affected leaves turn reddish brown and bronzy.

diagnosis_line: An insect pest was found on the tomato plant: Root-knot nematode (Meloidogyne spp.).

llama.raw_text: Root-knot nematodes cause root galls on the feeder roots and sometimes affect the entire root system showing heavy galling. This affects the uptake of nutrition and water and the plants show wilting during warmer part of the day. This causes stunted plants with yellow foliage resulting in yield reduction.

dropped_sentences: Leaves with serpentine mines dry and drop off.

Serpentine-shaped tunnels are formed in the leaf, indicating the path of feeding by the maggots. Apply neem cake to the furrows at 250 kg/ha at planting and again after 25 days.

diagnosis_line: An insect pest was found on the tomato plant: Thrips.

dropped_sentences: Thrips suck the sap from tomato plants.
llama.raw_text: Thrips suck the sap from tomato plants. Silvery streaks appear on the leaf surface. Pre-mature dropping of flowers occurs. Bud necrosis happens. Thrips are the vector of tomato spotted wilt virus. Use locally available empty tins painted blue and coated with grease, vaseline, or castor oil. Plant 5-6 rows of sorghum or maize around the field as a barrier crop.

diagnosis_line: An insect pest was found on the tomato plant: Whitefly (Bemisia tabaci).

llama.raw_text: Chlorotic spots. Yellowing. Downward curling and drying of leaves. Whitefly is a well-known vector, which transmits tomato leaf curl virus. Whiteflies also excrete honeydew, causing sooty mold.

diagnosis_line: Diagnosis: Tomato leaf curl virus on a tomato leaf (model confidence 92%). Estimated spread on the photographed leaf: medium.

llama.raw_text: Severe stunting of plants. Downward rolling and crinkling of the leaves; older leaves become leathery and brittle. Shortened internodes and more side branches give a bushy appearance. The virus is spread by whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci). Leaves show downward rolling, curling, twisting, and chlorosis. Plants show stunting, shortening of internodes, bushy appearance, no flowering, and fruiting at later stage of virus infection. Sometimes leaves show light and dark mottle symptoms.
